text:
mike: hey folks - accepted the org invite but when I try to push I get a 403. I added my work SSH key to my work GH account, but `ssh -T` still shows my personal account. I also see two entries in macOS Keychain for github.com and I'm not sure which token is being used. who should I ping? cc @anya

anya: welcome mike! that sounds like an ssh-agent/keychain + gh auth mix. can you paste `ssh -T git@github.com`, `git remote -v`, and `gh auth status` outputs?

mike: sure:
```
$ ssh -T git@github.com
Hi mike.personal! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.
$ git remote -v
origin	git@github.com:redwood-inference/console.git (fetch)
origin	git@github.com:redwood-inference/console.git (push)
$ gh auth status
Logged in to github.com as mike.personal (GitHub.com)
```
I definitely uploaded `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work.pub` to my `mike-work` account and accepted the invite as `mike-work`. Not sure why my machine prefers the personal key.

it-support: thanks. common culprits: 1) ssh-agent is offering your personal key first, 2) `~/.ssh/config` missing Host alias or IdentitiesOnly, so multiple keys get tried and GitHub picks the first that matches (personal). 3) Credential helpers for HTTPS can still cache tokens but your remotes are SSH so agent keys are the main issue. Two quick fixes: a) use an SSH host alias and set IdentityFile for that alias, b) force IdentitiesOnly yes so ssh won't try keys from the agent. Example config to add to `~/.ssh/config`:
```
Host github-work
  HostName github.com
  User git
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work
  IdentitiesOnly yes
```
Then change repo remote to `git@github-work:redwood-inference/console.git`. That will ensure the work key is used.

mike: I tried adding the config but I still get `Hi mike.personal` from `ssh -T git@github-work` - maybe the agent is forwarding the personal key anyway.

it-support: if your agent loaded the personal key you can remove it from the agent (ssh-add -D to remove all keys, then ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work). Also check macOS Keychain: some users have `ssh-add -K` entries or the system-level Keychain storing old identities. Try `ssh-add -l` to list agent keys, then `ssh-add -D` and re-add the work key only. After that `ssh -T git@github-work` should greet `mike-work`.

mike: `ssh-add -l` showed three keys including id_rsa (personal). ran `ssh-add -D` then `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work` and `ssh -T git@github-work` now says `Hi mike-work!` Nice. But pushing still fails with 403 when I push to origin (which I still have set to git@github.com...).

it-support: you'll need to update the remote to point at the host alias so the right key is used for pushes. Run:
```
git remote set-url origin git@github-work:redwood-inference/console.git
```
Then try `git push`. If you still get 403, double-check that `mike-work` is actually a member of the org and that SSO is enforced. `gh api orgs/redwood-inference/memberships/mike-work` will indicate membership.

mike: updated remote and pushed but got `Permission denied (publickey).` I can `ssh -T git@github-work` successfully though.

it-support: two possibilities: 1) the repo ACLs restrict push to specific teams and your account isn't on that team yet, 2) the push attempt may still be using an HTTPS fallback somewhere (CI hooks or submodules) or you have an old credential cached in Keychain for https://github.com that some tooling uses. Check `git push --verbose` for clues and `gh api repos/redwood-inference/console/collaborators/mike-work` to see if you have push permission.

mike: `gh api repos/redwood-inference/console/collaborators/mike-work` returns 404. `gh api orgs/redwood-inference/memberships/mike-work` returns "role: member, state: active" though. Weird.

it-support: interesting - membership active but not a collaborator on that repo. Many repos in org are team-restricted. I'll add you to the `console-team`. Give me your GitHub username to confirm (mike-work?).

mike: `mike-work` yes

it-support: adding mike-work to console-team and grant push. Also removing stale Keychain github.com entries we found earlier.

gh-bot: Added mike-work to team console-team in redwood-inference (role: member).

mike: pushed successfully after team add. thank you! couple follow-ups: 1) how do I avoid this headache when setting up a new laptop? 2) any onboarding doc notes I should check?

anya: great questions. Short checklist for new machines: - create a dedicated work SSH key pair, - add work key to work GH account before accepting invites, - add SSH Host alias with IdentitiesOnly yes, - avoid auto-loading personal keys in ssh-agent (don't run `ssh-add -K` for personal keys), - clear Git credential helper entries for github.com before `gh auth login`, - run `gh auth login` and `ssh -T` to confirm identity, - verify org email and complete SSO so membership is enforced. We'll add a short bullet list to the onboarding doc.

it-support: adding a ticket to docs to include an SSH walk-through and keychain troubleshooting tips. Also note: macOS Keychain can auto-insert HTTPS tokens; if you use HTTPS in any flows, clear Keychain entries named "github.com" and re-run `gh auth login`.

security-bot: reminder: work keys should be protected with a passphrase and stored on secure machines only. If you use hardware-backed keys (YubiKey), prefer that for higher security.

mike: thanks everyone. resolved for me. leaving a tip: if you see unexpected account names in `ssh -T`, run `ssh-add -l` and `ssh-add -D` early in setup; that would've saved me 30min.

it-support: closing thread - resolved. :white_check_mark:
